messages:
Eve: Quick RFC follow-up — after last week's kernel RFC meeting we need a concrete plan for integrating Triton kernels and CUTLASS/CUDA fallbacks into the runtime. High level goals: expose a kernel-adapter surface, make selection perf-driven, and keep packaging simple.

Marcus: Agreed. We should avoid shipping huge binary sets by default. Proposal: runtime picks implementation based on op type + sequence-length profile + hardware tier. Keep the decision logic pluggable.

Priya: Important callout on attention variants — flash attention style kernels (Triton) beat GEMM-based CUTLASS for short-to-medium seqs, but for long sequences or fp16 math CUTLASS sometimes wins. Also need to think about kv-cache memory layout changes.

ci-bot: Perf snapshot uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/bench/1799989000 — short summary: Triton custom-attn wins for seq < 1024 on A100 and L4, CUTLASS mm wins for seq > 2048 on A100. Mixed results on L4 for tiled kernels. Full CSV attached to the run.

Yun: Can we get a small, consistent microbench harness per kernel? I can own that. Need to control seq lengths, batch sizes, and pinned allocations.

Dmitri: Sketch of adapter interface I'd propose (pseudo):

```text
interface KernelAdapter {
  supports(op_signature): bool
  estimate_cost(op_signature, hw): float
  run(op_context): Result
}
```

We need to design stable ABI boundaries, lightweight cost estimation, and a safe fallback path for failures. Also need a version field on adapters so we can roll forward/back.

Eve: Action items (owners + ETA):
- design adapter interface + RFC (Dmitri) - due in 1 week
- microbench harness + initial matrix (Yun) - due in 5 days
- packaging impact analysis (Marcus) - due in 3 days
- CI gating rule for kernel changes (Priya) - due in 1 week
- prototype: triton-attn + cutlass-mm combo (Eve + Marcus) - due in 3 weeks

Priya: For CI gating I suggest: auto-accept if perf regression < 2% vs baseline; otherwise block and require manual signoff. Also require deterministic outputs for numeric-stability tests.

Marcus: Memory-format note: canonicalize KV layout at runtime boundary so adapters can assume a common input. That minimizes conversions inside hot kernels. This reduces per-kernel complexity and binary size.

Eve: We also need a runtime fallback policy when a kernel crashes or OOMs: immediate retry with next-best adapter, capture telemetry event including op_signature and hw, and degrade gracefully (throttle or reject) if repeated failures.

ci-bot: Created issue tickets: #INF-2312 (adapter-rfc), #INF-2313 (microbench-harness), #INF-2314 (ci-gating-kernels).

Dmitri: I'll draft the RFC tonight and ping for early review. One unresolved question: should adapter decision be per-request (fine-grained) or per-batch (amortized)? My leaning is per-batch to keep CPU overhead low.

Yun: Per-batch is cheaper to compute and cacheable. For highly heterogeneous seq-length workloads we can do per-sub-batch or hot-path cache keyed by seq-distribution. Start with per-batch + hot cache.

Eve: Good plan. I'll sync with infra to reserve A100 and L4 nodes for benchmark runs next Tue. Please add sample configs to the microbench so we can reproduce.

Marcus: I'll handle packaging notes and outline a slim runtime artifact vs full artifact strategy.

Priya: Noted. I'll draft CI gating rules and small numeric-stability tests.

Eve: Thanks all — follow-ups on the tickets. :thumbsup:

Dmitri: Will post RFC link when ready.

Marcus: :white_check_mark: closing loop tomorrow EOD for packaging plan.

Priya: ack, will have CI draft by then.
